title: Picking the Best Option by Logic | Principles of Management Ep 23
description:
How do you pick the best option when everyone disagrees? All five Chai Corner outlets need fresh milk, three dairies want the deal, and Kabir, Asha and Meena each want a different one. In this animated lesson, Ravi drops the guessing and uses pure logic.

You will learn what rational decision making means (using logic to choose the option with the most value), meet the perfect decision maker economists call economic man, and see what optimising means. Then we build Ravi's score sheet live through all six steps: define the problem, pick the criteria, weight them, list the alternatives, rate each one, and compute the totals. We look at the model's four big assumptions, see clear criteria, weights, open bids, scoring and optimising at work today in a hospital, a hiring team, a city and an airline, and look at the human side honestly: the logic is clear and fair, but facts cost time and money, the assumptions rarely hold, and changing the weights changes the winner.

This is Episode 23 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Three dairies, one deal
0:23 Every fact Ravi can find
0:35 What is rational decision making?
1:01 The six steps, live on a score sheet
1:57 The four big assumptions
2:13 The rational model at work today
2:45 The human side of pure logic
3:18 Quick check
3:32 Recap

Next episode: Bounded Rationality.
